text:
Dmitry Orlov is 35, a Stanley Cup winner with Washington in 2018, and he is having a productive month. He has 9 points in his last ten games, including a four-point night in Utah on Nov. 14. San Jose Hockey Now ran a piece titled "Orlov & Marchment Finding Their Games."

Our numbers are cautious. At his ice time, we'd expect about 4.6 points over those ten games, and his own chances haven't changed. He has 3 goals on 1.09 expected goals, the quality of his shots, and his scoring rate is well above the top of our talent range for him. More than half his points, 8 of 14, came on the power play, and Evolving-Hockey credited most of his modest 2025-26 value to the power play.

Five-on-five is the concern. San Jose has had only about 41% of the chance quality with him on the ice, worse than without him, and his ice time is down two and a half minutes a night over this stretch. One bright spot from Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: he stops 15% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%.
headline: Dmitry Orlov's hot stretch is mostly bounces
